title: Prompt Microkernel Orchestration — sketch
content:
Context
-----
Quick personal sketch for a tiny runtime "microkernel" that composes prompt transforms, validation, routing and local caching in a minimal API surface. Goal: make it trivial to add/new compose prompt-level behaviors (pre/post transforms, safety gates, metric hooks) without touching serving runtime or client SDKs.

Notes-to-self (why):
- We already have heavy orchestration in the serving layer; that's great for scheduling/allocs but heavy to instrument for prompt-level logic.
- Many teams want custom pre/post logic (persona snippets, privacy scrubbing, deidentify, `prepend system` adjustments, sampling overrides) but small surface to change.
- A microkernel collocated with requester (or as a light sidecar) gives low-latency transforms and unified policy enforcement.

Core concepts (v0)
-----------------
- Kernel: tiny process that owns a pipeline of prompt plugins (sources: local files, remote bundles, policy store). Exposes a single HTTP/gRPC endpoint: /v1/transform.
- Plugin: composable stateless function (init config, transform(request) -> result). Plugins can be JS/wasm/Python sandboxed.
- Bundle: ordered collection of plugins + metadata + conditional routing rules. A bundle can be referenced by id in a request.
- Decision: do NOT attempt to run heavy evals or model inference in kernel. Only transforms, heuristics, caches, and routing decisions.

API shape (sketch, JSON-over-HTTP)
---------------------------------
POST /v1/transform
Request body (application/json):
{
  "bundle_id": "string|optional",      // pre-configured pipeline
  "plugins": ["inline-plugin-ids"],   // optional override pipeline
  "input": {
    "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"..."}],
    "meta": {"client_request_id":"...", "tenant":"acme"}
  },
  "mode": "sync|async|dry-run",
  "trace_id": "..."
}

Response (sync):
{
  "ok": true,
  "output": {
    "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"... after transforms ..."}],
    "metadata": {"applied_plugins":["deid","persona-attach"], "cache_hit":false}
  },
  "diagnostics": ["plugin-x-lint:warn: length > 8k"]
}

Notes on API: keep it intentionally minimal. Clients should not need to know plugin internals beyond bundle ids. Dry-run mode returns what would happen without side effects.

Plugin model (informal)
-----------------------
- Interface:
  - init(config) -> token/handle
  - transform(input, ctx) -> { output, diagnostics }  // synchronous fast path
  - maybe async hooks for remote lookups
- Safety: sandboxed, resource-constrained (cpu, mem, time). Compute budget default: 50ms CPU for transform.
- Language: Wasm is preferred for portability, fallback to a restricted JS runtime for quick iteration.

Example plugin config (YAML-ish)
--------------------------------
- id: persona-attach
  type: inline
  runtime: wasm
  config:
    persona_snippet_id: "sales-lite"
    insertion: prefix_system
    conditions:
      - client_tier in ["free","trial"] -> apply_suggestion_footer: false

- id: pii-scrub
  runtime: wasm
  type: remote
  config:
    ruleset: "redwood-pii-v2"
    redact_mask: "[REDACTED]"
    allowed_fields: ["email_hash"]

Execution model/ordering rules
------------------------------
1) bundle-level prefilters (fast regex/whitelist) — if fail -> return 400 or route to fallback.
2) ordered plugin transforms (deterministic ordering; stable ids)
3) post-checks: token_count_estimate, safety heuristic, policy audit log append
4) optional callout: route request to serving runtime with hint headers (e.g., deterministic cache key)

Caching & prefix reuse idea
---------------------------
- Cache key = hash(bundle_id|plugin_config_snapshot|normalized_prompt)
- Support partial prefix reuse: if cache stores tokenized prefix -> server can warm KV cache for generation.
- Microkernel returns a warm-hint header: "x-warm-prefix-id: abc123" which the serving runtime understands.

Architecture ASCII (simple)
---------------------------
[Client] -> [Sidecar Kernel] -> [Serving API]
                 |                 ^
                 |-> local cache ---|
                 |-> policy store (optional remote)

Failure modes and graceful degradation
-------------------------------------
- If kernel fails to respond within deadline -> pass through original input with best-effort headers and mark "kernel_unavailable" metric.
- If individual plugin errors -> depending on plugin config: fail fast / skip / return warning in diagnostics.
- Version skew: bundle snapshots are immutable; kernel keeps a small GC of snapshots. Any bundle mismatch should fall back to a server-side bundle id.

Observability hooks
-------------------
- Per-request: applied_plugins, timing per plugin, cache_hit, rule_triggers
- Metrics: plugin_error_rate, avg_transform_latency, cache_hit_rate
- Traces: attach transform span to existing trace_id.

Security considerations
-----------------------
- Plugins run in sandbox with no outbound network unless explicitly allowed (callouts should be whitelisted per-bundle).
- Sensitive data redaction enforced as policy plugin with highest priority; kernels must support policy override require flag for enterprise customers.
- Audit logs persisted to customer's configured sink; kernel only stores minimal operation logs.

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- Should microkernel be a sidecar or a library that can be embedded? Sidecar easier for ops, library easier for unit tests.
- How to sign/verify bundles? We need a signing scheme to prevent tampering (JWT-ish + bundle manifest hash).
- Plugin dev UX: local dev loop should support JS shim -> wasm compile automatically.
- Cost model: if kernels are deployed on customer infra (private), ensure we meter plugin runtime for billing? probably not in v1.
- Can we get away with only wasm? Some teams love python for rules — maybe allow remote webhook plugin type with strict quotas.

Draft rollout plan (v0 -> v1)
------------------------------
- v0: prototype sidecar with 4 built-in plugins (pii-scrub, persona, length-trunc, header-inject). No user-auth bundles. Run as opt-in on dev-only clusters.
- v0.1: add bundle signing, dry-run mode, observability hooks (Prometheus + trace).
- v1: allow tenant bundles stored in control-plane, RBAC for bundle publishing, and wasm-sandbox multi-tenant isolation.

References / links in head
-------------------------
- wasm runtime notes: https://bytecodealliance.org/
- similar idea: nginx lua hook / envoy ext_proc for lightweight transforms -> review ext_proc patterns

One-pager action items (for next sync)
-------------------------------------
- [ ] sketch API proto and wire format (Marco)
- [ ] prototype wasm plugin loader and noop transform (Evelyn)
- [ ] add telemetry schema to Observability backlog (me)
- [ ] draft bundle manifest signing proposal (security)

Random notes / brain dump
------------------------
- Might be worth modeling plugin ordering as a small DSL: if(condition)->pluginA->else->pluginB. But that gets into complexity; prefer simple ordered lists + conditional flags.
- Think about multi-tenant cache eviction: namespace by tenant id to avoid leakage.
- Consider a "cost-hint" metadata field so serving runtime can choose cheaper model variant when the kernel indicates heavy prompt expansion.

End of sketch.
